boards.title: Your First Weekend at Skidmore College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe first-weekend sequence using recurring campus places, arts, outdoors, and student activities.

cards.title: Start on Case Green
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • campus gathering point
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or simply pause here after unpacking. Use the open lawn as a low-pressure place to orient yourself and say hello to classmates.
cards.short_summary: Begin with an outdoor pause at a central campus green.
cards.evidence_claim: Skidmore identifies Case Green as a location for new-student orientation gatherings, including an evening welcome program.
cards.source_title: Welcome Class of 2029: New Student Orientation
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; check the College calendar for scheduled programming.

cards.entity_name: Frances Young Tang Teaching Museum and Art Gallery
cards.title: See what is on view at the Tang
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • campus art stop
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries at your own pace, then use a work that catches your attention as an easy conversation starter with a new friend.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided art break on Skidmore’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tang Teaching Museum is on Skidmore’s campus, is free and open to all, and does not require a reservation for general admission.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; Thursday hours extend to 9 p.m.; closed Mondays and major holidays.

cards.title: Regroup at Burgess Café
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Case Center
cards.notes: Pick up a snack or drink if you want one, then take a few minutes to compare weekend plans and campus tips with your new group.
cards.short_summary: A casual Case Center stop for a snack and planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Burgess Café is on the second floor of Case Center and offers coffee, tea, pastries, snacks, sandwiches, sushi, and grab-and-go items.
cards.access_notes: The College lists weekday service; confirm current dining hours before going.

cards.title: Make Scribner Library familiar
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • central campus
cards.notes: Find the entrance, a comfortable floor, and the service points before classes accelerate. Save the route so returning for a book or study session feels easy.
cards.short_summary: A quick orientation stop in Skidmore’s library.
cards.evidence_claim: Skidmore describes Lucy Scribner Library as being at the heart of campus and lists public printing there during scheduled hours.
cards.access_notes: Access and services follow the library’s scheduled hours; verify the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Take a daylight North Woods walk
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • on-campus trail network
cards.notes: Choose a daylight walk, stay on marked trails, and use the posted trail map. This is a gentle reset before the day’s social and campus activities.
cards.short_summary: Explore Skidmore’s on-campus hardwood forest by trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Skidmore describes the North Woods as a network of trails through 155 acres of hardwood forest on campus.
cards.access_notes: Use the trail map and daylight conditions; wear suitable footwear and stay on established routes.

cards.title: Browse Club Fair tables
cards.subtitle: First Friday of fall or spring semester • campus activity
cards.notes: Make one pass without pressure to commit. Ask current members what beginners can expect, take only the information you will actually revisit, and note follow-up dates.
cards.short_summary: Meet student organizations and collect a few realistic next steps.
cards.evidence_claim: Skidmore says Club Fair is held twice yearly on the first Friday of the fall and spring semesters and is a campus tradition for exploring clubs.
cards.access_notes: This is a semester-specific recurring event; confirm its date and location through Student Life.

cards.title: Ask about an Outing Club trip
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • student outdoor activity
cards.notes: Check the club’s current SkidSync listings, choose a trip matched to your experience, and ask leaders about required preparation and equipment before registering.
cards.short_summary: Connect with a student group that organizes outdoor activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Skidmore states that Outing Club provides hiking, climbing, canoeing, swimming, and camping activities for all levels of outdoor interest and ability.
cards.access_notes: Activity details, registration, and any equipment requirements are set by the current club listing.

cards.title: Check the Zankel performance calendar
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening • campus music venue
cards.notes: Look at the current program, choose an event that interests you, and review its ticket details and audience policies before inviting someone along.
cards.short_summary: Find a live music or arts event at Skidmore’s dedicated venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Arthur Zankel Music Center hosts programming throughout the academic year and includes the 600-seat Helen Filene Ladd Concert Hall and 58-seat Elisabeth Luce Moore Hall.
cards.access_notes: Programs and ticket requirements vary; consult the current event listing before attending.

cards.title: Share Saturday dinner at Murray-Aikins
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening • campus dining
cards.notes: Meet a few people for dinner, then linger only if it feels comfortable. Use the meal as a practical chance to trade course questions and Sunday plans.
cards.short_summary: A sit-down campus dinner stop before the evening continues.
cards.evidence_claim: Murray-Aikins Dining Hall serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner on weekends, with dinner listed from 5 to 8 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Weekend dinner is listed 5–8 p.m.; meal plans, Skid card, debit, and credit card are accepted as applicable.

cards.title: Finish with a low-key recreation plan
cards.subtitle: Sunday • Williamson Sports Center
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule, then try an informal activity you already enjoy or simply learn where the facilities are for a later visit with friends.
cards.short_summary: Locate the recreation center and plan a future active break.
cards.evidence_claim: Skidmore states that Williamson Sports Center is open during the school year for informal running, swimming, weight training, racquetball, basketball, indoor soccer, and aerobics.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and activity availability depend on the current recreation schedule and College eligibility rules.
